options: The smallest particle of an element that is still that element
A large clump of bonded elements
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that still behaves like that element — split it further and you lose the element.
questions.misconception: Molecules are made of atoms (not the other way around), and atoms are matter, not energy — the atom is the smallest particle that keeps its element's identity.

options: A nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons in shells around it
Only protons and electrons, no neutrons
A solid marble of uniform material
questions.explanation: An atom has a nucleus (protons + neutrons) at its center and electrons orbiting in shells around it.
questions.misconception: An atom is NOT a solid ball — it has a dense nucleus with protons and neutrons, and electrons orbiting far outside in shells.

questions.explanation: Atoms are mostly empty space — the nucleus is tiny and the electrons are tiny, with vast emptiness between them.
questions.misconception: Atoms feel solid only because huge numbers of them are packed together — inside each one, the nucleus and electrons leave mostly empty space.

questions.prompt: What do atoms build when they bond together?
questions.explanation: Atoms bond together to build molecules — like two hydrogens and one oxygen bonding into a water molecule.
questions.misconception: Electrons, nuclei, and protons are parts of the atom, not things atoms build — atoms BUILD molecules when they bond.
